extracted.intended_audience: beginning improvisers and aspiring sketch writers (new Second City students)
extracted.subtask_description: A weekend program condensing the first levels of Second City's Improv and Writing programs into three classes, teaching foundational improv skills and core sketch-creation concepts for beginners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basics of Second City improv
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the basics of Second City improv—yes, and, being in the moment, and character POV
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foundational improv syllabus element: introduces core practices (agreement, presence, character-based scene work) that students are expected to learn and apply during short-form and long-form improv exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yes, and
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle of agreement and contribution: accept offers from scene partners and add new information to move scenes forward; an essential collaborative mindset in improv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Being in the moment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus and presence: attend to immediate stimuli and partner choices instead of pre-planning; supports truthful reactions and stronger scene work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character POV
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work from a character's perspective to drive choices and stakes in a scene; helps create distinct, believable characters and coherent scene logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core concepts of Second City sketch creation
rubrics_metrics.description: the core concepts of Second City sketch creation—creating from abundance, collaboration, character development and joke structure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level sketch-writing goals for the program: emphasizes generative idea work, collaborative authorship, developing characters for sketches, and constructing jokes within sketch frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating from abundance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative generation strategy: prioritize creating many ideas and materials rather than scarcity; encourages exploration and iterating on plentiful concepts to find strong comedic material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration (in writing and improv)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes group authorship and ensemble-driven creation—sharing, building on others' ideas, and co-writing as part of making sketches and improv scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character development (for sketches)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop memorable, specific characters whose perspectives and desires drive sketch situations and jokes; a focus of the writing curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke structure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study of how jokes are constructed within sketches (setups, beats, punchlines, callbacks) to create comedic payoff and shape sketch rhythm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated Improv + Writing approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn both aspects of the Second City approach to comedy with our Winter Intensive!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program intentionally combines improv fundamentals and sketch-writing concepts so students practice generative improv skills and translate them into written sketch work within an intensive weekend format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program intensity / structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Second City Winter Intensive condenses the first levels of our Improv Program and our Writing Program into three classes in one weekend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation-setting criterion: the course is an accelerated format (multiple long sessions across a weekend) covering beginner material from two programs; students should be prepared for concentrated training and rapid skill application.
